items.summary: The bacterial flagellum is a motility organelle that enables bacteria to swim and is composed of more than 30 different proteins. items.title: Protecting the vulnerable Y chromosome at the beginning of development
items.summary: It's known that the Y chromosome, which confers male sex, plays a big role in development and health, despite its small size. As cells age they frequently lose their Y chromosomes, which is associated with conditions like cancer, Alzheimer's disease and heart disease.

items.summary: Geologists have uncovered new evidence that dramatic sea-level changes carved giant underwater canyons in South Australia's Flinders Ranges hundreds of millions of years ago, helping to create conditions that preserved some of the earliest complex life on Earth. items.title: Removing too much crop waste for bioenergy could come at a cost to biodiversity, study finds
items.summary: Crop residues—the stems, leaves and husks left behind after harvesting cereals—could provide an important source of renewable energy for Europe, but research led by the University of Surrey suggests that removing too much from fields could come at a cost to biodiversity.

items.title: Two genes, two harvests: Adapting barley for double cropping
items.summary: Growing two crops in succession on the same land requires a tight schedule. In parts of central and eastern China, farmers sow barley in autumn and harvest it in late spring. items.title: The migration that remade Africa
items.summary: It's not easy to extract iron from its ore. But the peoples of the ancient city of Great Zimbabwe—the capital of a thriving kingdom in southern Africa between A.D. 1000 and 1700—were masters.

items.title: COP31 opens with leaders under pressure to tackle climate crisis
items.summary: The COP31 climate talks kicked off Monday with an early fight over money as the U.N.'s chief urged world leaders to "get serious" about tackling the crisis after a year of devastating weather extremes.

items.summary: The brilliant magenta feathers on the head and throat of a male Anna's hummingbird present an optical puzzle. Magenta cannot be produced by a single wavelength of light. items.title: CT scanning the centuries-old head of Jeremy Bentham
items.summary: Cutting-edge medical imaging techniques have revealed that Jeremy Bentham, the Georgian philosopher and reformer, suffered from chronic toothache and a jaw riddled with arthritis.
